subject: Post-demo model shortlist & next steps

Subject: Post-demo: model shortlist & next steps

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and the recommended next steps after the demo:

What we heard
- Primary goal: clinical triage assistant to summarize patient intake notes and surface follow-up questions for nurses.
- P95 latency target: <= 350ms token-service for 512-token responses.
- Throughput: ~250 requests/min during peak clinic hours.
- Strict PHI handling; prefer Private deployment (VPC) or Dedicated with KMS.

Recommended model shortlist (initial candidates) — rationale below:
1) Mistral-Instant-7B (quantized) — Best latency/cost balance for classification & short-form summarization. Good instruction-following; cheap to run at scale.
2) Llama-3-13B-Instruct (8-bit/4-bit quant) — Strong quality for longer summaries and nuanced clinical context; higher cost but fewer quality regressions for edge cases.
3) Falcon-40B-Instruct (pruned + F32 kernels) — Highest quality for complex clinical reasoning, useful as a fallback for critical cases; higher latency/cost.

Attached: acme_model_shortlist.xlsx (concise benchmark table), acme_eval_prompts.txt (initial prompt set we used in the demo), benchmark_report_v1.pdf (detailed latency/cost data).

Next steps (proposed)
- You: confirm priority evaluation scenarios (summarization vs question generation vs triage routing).
- Redwood: run a 3-day private eval across the shortlisted models using your sample dataset (we'll need redacted sample records).
- Neha (cc): will share a proposed eval plan + infra checklist and a security/compliance note for PHI handling.

Benchmarks and links:
- Short benchmark summary (attached) — costs are estimated per 1M tokens; latency is P95 measured on a c6-gpu class.
- Detailed results: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cD-example-benchmarks
- Prompt set (editable): https://gist.github.com/marissa/acme-eval-prompts

Open concerns
- Quality regressions: we recommend running targeted regression evals on our prompt sets when model versions change. We'll include a monitoring hook for hallucination and factuality drift.
- Model compatibility with your on-prem EHR extract pipeline — we may need a lightweight adapter for tokenization differences.

Would love confirmation on which two models you'd like us to prioritize for the private eval. I recommend Mistral-Instant-7B for cost/latency, and Llama-3-13B for quality-sensitive triage.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference

Emma — great, thanks for the confirmation. Quick answers here and an ask for the redacted sample format: 

Cost delta (very approximate) for 60M tokens/month: 
- Mistral-Instant-7B (quantized): ~$0.12k/month per 1M tokens => ~ $7,200/month
- Llama-3-13B (8-bit): ~$0.40k/month per 1M tokens => ~ $24,000/month
Notes: these include compute and model licensing estimates for Dedicated capacity. Exact numbers depend on batching and KV cache hit rates; we can instrument during the eval.

Eval plan (Neha will take lead):
- Run parallel 72-hour eval on your redacted dataset across top-2 models.
- Metrics: ROUGE/EM for summarization, precision/recall for question-generation intent, latency (P50/P95), cost per 1M tokens, and hallucination rate (manual sample + automated checks).
- Deliverable: dashboard + per-case examples + recommended production profile (quantization and batching config).

Neha — can you attach the eval checklist and a template for the redacted sample (we should confirm PHI masking rules and transfer method)?

Emma/Carlos — I'll also share a short SOW/PO terms doc to get procurement started. HubSpot link to deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/ACME-1001

Thanks —
Marissa
